documents.title: SHSU Generative AI Guidance
documents.stance_why: The page states 'there is no defining university policy on AI' and 'It is up to each instructor to specify an AI policy for that particular class', so it sets no stance itself and hands the decision to instructors; it offers no named tiers.
documents.summary: A resource page with separate guidance for students, faculty and staff. It defers AI rules to each instructor, ties unauthorized or undisclosed use to the Academic Honesty Policy, cautions against AI detectors, and tells staff to use approved tools and protect data.

units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this. 'It is important to learn how and when to use AI' is a principle statement in the student guide, a real policy statement; nearest type P44 with B's fit_note.

The source says 'the simple use of generative AI is not necessarily an academic integrity problem'; it grants no default permission, so P02 would be a stretch. units.policy: A student's undisclosed use of generative AI in assignments outside the boundaries that an instructor has set for a specific course may constitute a violation of SHSU's Academic Honesty policy.

units.resolution_why: A coded P28, informs; B coded P36, must-not. The source says 'undisclosed use of generative AI in assignments outside the boundaries that an instructor has set ... may constitute a violation': a may-statement (informs), not a prohibition. P36 already carries the generic unauthorized-use unit; this sentence names undisclosed use as the violation, so P28, with A's fit_note that both undisclosed and out-of-bounds are required.

units.why: Passage: While there is no defining university policy on AI Final codes UNCOVERED, admin, general, informs; see resolution_why for how the coders' codes were reconciled.

units.policy: There is no defining university policy on AI; SHSU works to integrate AI practice into existing and proposed policies such as Academic Honesty and Course Structure and Management.

The source says 'there is no defining university policy on AI' while integrating AI into existing policies; P56 sets a framework, which this denies. Final UNCOVERED with B's note (a recurring pattern worth reviewing between batches).

units.why: 'an emergent mandate from the state: integrate AI into classroom learning and student research projects' for workforce readiness gives the career rationale, so P44.
units.anchor: integrate AI into classroom learning and student research projects to help prepare students
units.policy: The university has an emergent mandate from the state to integrate AI into classroom learning and student research projects to help prepare students for workforce readiness.
units.fit_note: A state mandate to integrate AI, not only a statement that AI is a professional skill. A state mandate to integrate AI into classes and student research for workforce readiness, not a course teaching AI as a skill.

units.why: 'we remain true to our foundational commitment to guiding students through their intellectual development and acquisition of personal academic skills' states the skill-building side of the balance, so P41.

units.anchor: examples of syllabus statements that cover different types of AI policies
units.policy: The page offers links to syllabus statement examples covering AI policies from a complete ban on AI tools to requiring AI tools for specific activities or assignments, many of which mention the rationale for the policy.
units.fit_note: Provides model statements for instructors; the document does not itself require a syllabus statement. Supplies sample syllabus statements across a ban-to-require range instead of stating who decides.
units.resolution_why: A coded modality informs, B may. 'The following links offer examples' provides resources and grants no permission, so informs. A's separate unit on 'Many of them also mention the rationale' (P66) is dropped as a description of linked examples and folded into this policy.

units.frag_end: conclusive evidence that they did not use AI.
units.policy: Instructors should be cautious in relying on an AI detection tool to take any negative actions regarding student work, since a student would have difficulty providing conclusive evidence that they did not use AI.
units.resolution_why: A coded modality should, unit_stance restrict; B should-not, neutral. 'Instructors should be cautious in relying on an AI detection tool to take any negative actions' discourages relying on detectors, so should-not; it says nothing restricting AI use, so neutral. P39 agreed.
